title: Ridge Regression Quiz
description: Test your understanding of ridge regression

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Ridge regression?
options: To make the model train faster
To prevent overfitting by adding a penalty for large coefficients
To select the most important features
To handle categorical variables
questions.explanation: Ridge regression adds an L2 penalty term (sum of squared coefficients) to the loss function. This penalty discourages large coefficients, which helps prevent overfitting and improves generalization to new data.

questions.question: What does the alpha (α) parameter control in Ridge regression?
options: The learning rate
The number of features to select
The strength of regularization
The number of training epochs
questions.explanation: Alpha controls the strength of regularization. Higher alpha values apply stronger penalties to large coefficients, shrinking them more toward zero. Alpha = 0 gives standard linear regression, while very large alpha heavily regularizes the model.

questions.question: How does Ridge regression handle coefficients compared to standard linear regression?
options: It sets some coefficients exactly to zero
It shrinks coefficients toward zero but keeps all features
It increases coefficient magnitudes
It doesn't affect coefficients at all
questions.explanation: Ridge regression shrinks all coefficients toward zero but never sets them exactly to zero. This means all features remain in the model, just with smaller coefficients. This is different from Lasso, which can set coefficients to exactly zero.

questions.question: Why is feature normalization especially important for Ridge regression?
options: It makes the model train faster
The L2 penalty treats all coefficients equally, so features should be on similar scales
It's not important for Ridge regression
It helps select important features
questions.explanation: The L2 penalty term sums the squared coefficients without considering feature scales. If features have different scales, the penalty will affect them unequally. Normalization ensures all features contribute fairly to the penalty term.

questions.question: What happens when alpha is set to 0 in Ridge regression?
options: The model fails to train
It becomes equivalent to standard linear regression
All coefficients become zero
It performs feature selection
questions.explanation: When alpha = 0, there is no regularization penalty, so the loss function becomes identical to standard linear regression. The model will fit the training data without any coefficient shrinkage.

questions.question: When should you use Ridge regression instead of standard linear regression?
options: When you have very few features
When you have many features or multicollinearity and want to prevent overfitting
When you need to select only a few important features
When your data has no noise
questions.explanation: Ridge regression is particularly useful when you have many features relative to samples, when features are correlated (multicollinearity), or when standard linear regression overfits. The regularization helps stabilize coefficient estimates and improves generalization.

questions.question: What is the L2 norm in the context of Ridge regression?
options: The sum of absolute values of coefficients
The square root of the sum of squared coefficients
The maximum coefficient value
The number of non-zero coefficients
questions.explanation: The L2 norm is the square root of the sum of squared coefficients: √(w₁² + w₂² + ... + wₙ²). It represents the magnitude of the weight vector and is the quantity that Ridge regression penalizes to keep coefficients small.

questions.question: How should you select the optimal alpha value for Ridge regression?
options: Always use alpha = 1
Use cross-validation to test different values and choose the one with best validation performance
Pick the largest alpha possible
Use the same alpha as the learning rate
questions.explanation: The optimal alpha depends on your specific dataset and problem. Cross-validation is the standard approach: try different alpha values, evaluate performance on validation data, and select the alpha that gives the best generalization. Common values to try include 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, and 100.

questions.question: What is a key difference between Ridge (L2) and Lasso (L1) regularization?
options: Ridge can set coefficients to exactly zero, Lasso cannot
Lasso can set coefficients to exactly zero, Ridge cannot
They are exactly the same
Ridge is faster than Lasso
questions.explanation: Lasso (L1) regularization can set coefficients to exactly zero, performing automatic feature selection. Ridge (L2) only shrinks coefficients toward zero but never makes them exactly zero, keeping all features in the model. This is a fundamental difference in how they regularize.
